# Explorer 0.53 career membership and construct review

Prepared October 19, 2026. This is an independent assistant content review of public occupation descriptions and the existing catalog, not a licensed assessment specialist's validation. No student records, account data, profiles, answers or application modules were changed by this task.

## Runtime-ready membership contract

The authoritative review is [explorer-053-field-review.json](../research/explorer-053-field-review.json): explicit entries for all 457 public occupation IDs, with fields, prior fields, reason, source description and source URL. Runtime must use this versioned explicit identity map. It must not rediscover fields by keywords, broad correlation, possible employer, shared source path or student selections.

Frozen SHA256: `51d65ad8e6343cf4fcfb6f90f062c28b7014feaae36b5170c55efac8216d27f2`. Inputs are hashed in the manifest. Changes to membership require a new reviewed artifact/amendment rather than silently rewriting this frozen record.

- **91 memberships changed** compared with the inherited mapping.
- **428 occupations have at least one reviewed field**;29 remain global-only with uncertainty.
- Global-only consists of 27 residual “All Other” aggregate categories and 2 religious vocations for which the twelve-field taxonomy lacks an adequate destination.
- Every 457 occupation remains discoverable globally. Global-only must not mean hidden, low-interest, ineligible or disliked.
- Apply membership **before** ranking and pagination. Validate it again when rendering field-survey main results. A global suggestion belongs on a separate explicit invitation/navigation.
- Membership organizes exploration. It does not demonstrate a student's interest, ability, training eligibility or capacity for a distinctive clinical/professional responsibility.

The baseline was existing expanded fieldIds or guided paths joined to careerFamilies. I screened the occupation identities/descriptions in all 12 fields, then made explicit exceptions. The legacy degree-inventory builder defaults unmatched occupations to Science; it places residual managers, financial/computer occupations, teachers and clinicians there. That fallback is not a defensible reviewed taxonomy. I also corrected broad SOC21 grouping and shared path leakage. [BLS SOC major groups](https://www.bls.gov/soc/2018/major_groups.htm) organize occupations; they do not validate these editorial fields as interest scales.

## Health: what changes and why

Health membership grows from 93 to 103, with 16 additions and 6 removals. The field includes clinical care, rehabilitation, mental/social support, population health, biomedical research, health information/systems and reviewed health-subject education. Card explanations must identify which kind of health work is involved; belonging to Health does not imply bedside care.

**Remove** generic social-science research assistants and food scientists: the former may work on any social research project; the latter studies food chemistry, production, safety and preservation, not the clinical dietetics role. Remove industrial-organizational psychologists, probation officers, clergy and religious-activity directors: shared psychology/helping language is insufficient to call them health professions. Industrial-organizational psychologists explicitly work on personnel/management/organizational problems. [O*NET definition](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/19-3032.00)

**Add** EMTs, school counselors, healthcare managers, clinical research coordinators, medical scientists, biomedical engineering, health informatics, clinical data management, biostatistics, bioinformatics, occupational health/safety and specific health/nursing/social-work teaching identities. Each has occupation-specific health content rather than a hypothetical hospital employer. Bioinformatics and biostatistics are explicitly research/data overlaps, not direct care. [Health informatics definition and tasks](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/15-1211.01), [medical scientists](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/19-1042.00), [biostatisticians](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/15-2041.01).

Generic software developers, data scientists, economists and food-production careers **remain outside Health**. A generic programmer can contribute to health work, but that possibility is not enough to substitute the generic occupation for a field-specific health result. Health Informatics Specialists is an actual reviewed interdisciplinary identity.

A field-only filter is necessary but not sufficient. A survey about counseling should not strongly label surgery because both belong to Health. The result service must still show which prior/new answers support the occupation, what specialty evidence remains missing, and whether the survey asked any relevant domain at all.

## Other scope corrections

- **Engineering/building:** retain all named source engineering/architecture occupations and add reviewed environmental, geospatial, logistics-engineering, resource-planning and energy-development overlaps. Generic “engineer” language in an IT or sales title is not a runtime inclusion rule. Biomedical engineering has explicit building/science/health membership.
- **Technology/data:** add actual digital-interface design, business intelligence, biostatistics, bioinformatics, GIS and quantitative/operations overlaps. Economic/quantitative research is not thereby health.
- **Science/environment:** preserve named natural/social-science occupations, add substantive scientific/quantitative overlaps, remove residual fallback aggregates and health-only residual categories. General social science remains discoverable here.
- **Business/law:** preserve source-defined business/legal roles; add explicit IT management, training/development, energy/production operations, research management and sustainability management overlaps. Prior-experience markers remain separate.
- **Teaching/learning:** coaching belongs here rather than creative arts; organizational training/development and specifically named health teaching are reviewed overlaps. Teaching a subject is not independent proof of wanting to practice that subject's profession.
- **Public safety:** probation, occupational prevention and reviewed security/environmental compliance overlaps are explicit. EMTs overlap with health.
- **Food/hospitality/personal care:** remove EMTs and dental assistants despite the old practical-service path; retain actual hospitality/personal services/facilities work. The present label under-describes facilities/grounds work: a later taxonomy/name review should make that scope visible rather than pretending janitorial work is food or personal care.
- **Transport/production:** add actual logistics analysis/engineering, transportation planning and energy-production operations. Survey questions need to distinguish logistics, physical transport, industrial operations and plant management.
- **Trades/repair and sales/office:** no automatic degree-role expansion. Existing specific occupations remain; general numeric/order interest is not enough to confirm an accounting/clerical occupation.

## Construct review: 24 original concepts, not 24 validated measures

[explorer-053-facet-review.json](../research/explorer-053-facet-review.json) reviews the 12 proposed domains and their two draft items. It lists exact existing O*NET specific-interest names, related knowledge/ability descriptors and restrictions.

[O*NET's content model](https://www.onetcenter.org/content.html) distinguishes interests, knowledge and abilities. Occupation ratings do not measure a student. The currently bundled specific-interest data includes AI/Expert provenance. Preserve rating dates/source/version; do not call a custom scenario-to-descriptor mapping externally validated.

| Draft domain | Possible specific-interest contexts | Main restriction |
|---|---|---|
| Understanding systems | No direct equivalent | Generic causal interest crosses physical, social, biological and computational systems. No single O*NET specific-interest area measures this. Require named occupation tasks/context before it supports a profession; use as invitation/explanation until reviewed task links exist. |
| Testing explanations | No direct equivalent | Experimental/evidential preference is a method, not a scientific subject or competence. Can describe general evidence-seeking interest, not confirm medicine/engineering/legal practice. A separate reviewed task link is needed for occupation-level ranking. |
| Quantitative patterns | Mathematics/Statistics | Closest semantic mapping to Mathematics/Statistics specific interest. General numerical/modeling interest can support broad quantitative connection. It does not establish mathematical ability or any specific analytical profession. |
| Design and constraints | Applied Arts and Design, Engineering | These are plausible design-method links but broad scenarios do not identify aesthetic/user-centered product design versus technical function. Keep one design domain; no independent double credit for the two items, and no automatic industrial-design/engineering confirmation. |
| Spatial/material exploration | Construction/Woodwork, Applied Arts and Design, Mechanics/Electronics | Split interpretation: picturing geometry and enjoying manual assembly are distinct. Neither answer measures spatial/manual ability. Spatial enjoyment alone must not imply liking heavy physical labor; material enjoyment must not infer engineering analysis. |
| Creative expression | Visual Arts, Creative Writing, Music, Performing Arts, Media | General expressive iteration; medium remains unknown. May support creative exploration but cannot confirm writing, music, acting, graphic design or illustration independently. Ask medium/context before specialty confirmation. |
| Direct personal support | Social Service, Health Care Service, Professional Advising | Social Service is the closest broad content link. Health Care Service is only contextual and must require actual health interest, not kindness. No diagnosis, distress tolerance, clinical care, counseling competence, or willingness for intimate bodily care is inferred. |
| Explanation and learning | Teaching/Education, Professional Advising | Teaching/Education has strong semantic relevance; general preference to explain can support education exploration. Does not identify age group, subject, classroom setting, developmental needs or teaching skill. |
| Initiative and negotiation | Business Initiatives, Management/Administration, Law, Professional Advising | Starting a shared activity and negotiating are related but distinct; do not infer business management, legal reasoning, sales persuasion or leadership ability from a generic team activity. Law is contextual only, not a direct default interest. |
| Organization and accuracy | Office Work, Accounting | General organization/information accuracy crosses nearly all professions. Office Work is plausible contextual link; accounting requires independent financial interest. Avoid converting liking order into accounting/clerical specialty confirmation or meticulousness ability. |
| Living systems and stewardship | Life Science, Nature/Outdoors, Agriculture | Biological inquiry and environmental stewardship are distinct. Living-world curiosity is not agriculture, animal care or clinical medicine. Waste-reduction interest also fits business/design/policy; route through reviewed occupations rather than field keyword assumptions. |
| Social systems and fairness | Social Science, Politics, Law | Social Science is the closest broad link. Interest in fairness is not proof of legal representation, adversarial argument, campaigning or social-work practice. Separate reasoning about rules from desire to advise/advocate personally. |

### Required interpretation rules

1. A preference answer never becomes an ability or knowledge score. Visualization, dexterity, reasoning, near vision or medical knowledge cannot be inferred from “love.” Use ability/knowledge descriptors for occupation explanation and optional learning/strength discussions only.
2. Generic systems thinking/testing explanations has no direct specific-interest equivalent. It may guide exploration across many disciplines; do not map it automatically to engineering, medical science, law or software confirmation.
3. Paired scenarios within a domain are not two independent confirmations. Cap domain contribution and retain coverage separately from mean preference.
4. Enjoying explaining is general teaching evidence, not proof of liking toddlers or classrooms. Enjoying personal support is not proof of willingness for diagnosis, intimate care or crisis exposure. Enjoying creative iteration does not identify the expressive medium.
5. Source descriptors currently retain top N elements; missing names are unknown/not selected, not zero interest and not a negative requirement. Use full source ratings for any numerical mapping and document thresholds before evaluation.
6. Broad official six-score correlation remains unchanged. A custom fine-grained score must be separately labeled experimental general-interest evidence, not an O*NET correlation, match probability or aptitude result.
7. Specific occupational reflections or reviewed tasks provide the necessary context for stronger evidence. Generic facet support can invite exploration at lower broad correlation without claiming a confirmed profession.
8. Preserve unknown/unfamiliar versus explicit dislike, answer provenance and original question identity. Do not reclassify historic generic answers as new distinct constructs.

## Checks for integration

- Assert the membership manifest has exactly 457 unique current IDs, only known fields and no unknown catalog references.
- Assert software/data-science/economics/food-science are not in Health; health informatics/clinical-data/biomedical/medical research/EMT identities are.
- For every field and every row on every page, assert entry.fields includes requested scope; test empty/negative/unfamiliar states never fall back globally.
- Verify global catalog and search retain all 29 global-only identities, with clear aggregate/context uncertainty and no automatic stronger label.
- Check occupation membership and student evidence independently: field inclusion alone never supplies an answer or confirmation.
- Freeze mappings and thresholds before model evaluation. Review changed individual offers subjectively, especially interdisciplinary labels; counts increasing is not accuracy evidence.
- Have a career-content specialist review these editorial exceptions before claiming expert-reviewed taxonomy or psychometric validity.
